findings.rationale: From round 11 onward CA's feature distribution shifts sharply (HighBP mean moves ~2 federation SDs; shift_sd 1.92 at round 11, ~2 thereafter), while rounds 1-10 are near zero shift. Its uploaded update jumps in norm (about 3.5x the median vs about 1.2x before) and turns strongly against the median (cos about -0.24 at round 11, down to -1.0 later), starting the same round. Its local AUC is normal (0.857 in c3, 0.825 in c15), so the anomaly comes from shifted data rather than a poisoned update. Its CITL is significantly negative (z about -4.7 to -4.8), consistent with the model under-predicting on drifted features. The same onset is seen in CO and WA.

CO's features shift from round 11 (shift_sd about 2.0-2.7 on HighBP/GenHlth/DiffWalk) with mean shift z about +5.1. Its updates grow to about 1.9x the median norm with strongly negative cosine (min_cos -0.85), and the anomaly is absent before round 11. Local AUC is normal (0.861 in c3, 0.822 in c15), so the data is drifted rather than the update poisoned. CITL is negative (z about -3.6 to -3.8), consistent with under-prediction on drifted inputs.

WA shows the strongest drift signal in the federation: from round 11 its feature means move about 2 SDs (GenHlth, HighBP, DiffWalk), with mean_shift_sd z about +10.9 and feature-level outliers (GenHlth p01 z_noise -8.96, DiffWalk p99 z_noise 11.5). Its update norm is about 2.9x the median with min cos -0.88, and the anomaly starts at round 11. Local AUC remains normal (0.831 in c3, 0.823 in c15). CITL is significantly negative (z about -4.6 to -4.7), consistent with drifted inputs.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of the update, performance, drift, feature, subgroup (Sex, AgeGroup, Income) and attribution tools, then confirmed leads with narrower queries. Three clients (CA, CO, WA) show a consistent drift fault starting at round 11: a feature-distribution shift of about 2 SD, update norms 2-3x the median with negative cosine beginning the same round, normal local AUC, and significantly negative CITL. I reported them as drift rather than poisoning because their local data is shifted while their performance is normal. Other leads (ND HighChol spread, DC BMI and age-group outcomes, WI and WV subgroup outliers, DE low AUC, GU and NC update statistics, NV and LA small norms) did not reproduce on re-query and were not reported. No free-rider, label-noise, prevalence-shift, subgroup-bias, missing-artefact or explanation-instability signal was confirmed. Budget is fully spent (20.0 epsilon).
